data.description:
## Description

What: Create plugins/dso/config/test-runners.yaml declaring each participating harness with its invocation method and a per-harness verdict-extraction adapter, and making the engine/wrapper distinction explicit — independent engines (bash-runner.sh, suite-engine.sh) versus wrappers (validate.sh -> bash-runner via test-batched.sh; run-hook-tests.sh -> suite-engine). The contract is asserted between engines; a wrapper is validated as producing its delegate engine's verdict or scope-annotated out. Record that 'bash-runner engine' in equivalence context means the test-batched.sh --runner=bash composite. Why: The equivalence test (sc-3) is manifest-driven; the manifest is the source of truth for invocation methods, adapters, and the engine/wrapper boundary. Scope IN: the manifest file with per-harness invocation method, per-harness adapter reference, and explicit engine-vs-wrapper classification. Scope OUT: the adapter implementations executing inside the test (sc-3), the path-filter derivation for the hook (sc-4), the classification-semantics doc reference (added in sc-5).

## Done Definitions

- plugins/dso/config/test-runners.yaml declares each participating harness with an invocation method and a verdict-extraction adapter ← Satisfies: sc-2
- The manifest explicitly classifies bash-runner.sh and suite-engine.sh as independent engines and validate.sh and run-hook-tests.sh as wrappers naming their delegate engine ← Satisfies: sc-2
- The manifest records that the bash-runner engine is invoked as the test-batched.sh --runner=bash composite ← Satisfies: sc-2

## Considerations

- [Boundary] plugins/dso/config/test-runners.yaml must be added to the plugin-boundary allowlist before first commit.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a runner-contract maintainer, I want a harness manifest declaring each engine and wrapper with its invocation method and verdict adapter, so that the equivalence contract knows what to run and how to normalize each engine's output.
